### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/driver-sql`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via needs_confirm (literal, a string literal in diffManagedTable; a string literal in isDeclaredRelaxPair; a string literal in isInstallRelaxation; a string literal in isPublishedColumnChange), relax_not_null (literal, a string literal in isDeclaredRelaxPair; a string literal in isInstallRelaxation; a string literal in isPublishedColumnChange))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via needs_confirm (literal, a string literal in diffManagedTable; a string literal in isDeclaredRelaxPair; a string literal in isInstallRelaxation; a string literal in isPublishedColumnChange))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 79d9c1435586d9b411b51a0ac395ea0c23dc3ddc` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `19710918a359f8b3a951a380226d0384992c1ae1` — the merge of head `f972c24ced205938213adc96316ec3b08d055b0f` into base `79d9c1435586d9b411b51a0ac395ea0c23dc3ddc`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 19710918a359f8b3a951a380226d0384992c1ae1 && git checkout 19710918a359f8b3a951a380226d0384992c1ae1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 79d9c1435586d9b411b51a0ac395ea0c23dc3ddc f972c24ced205938213adc96316ec3b08d055b0f && git checkout -B drift-repro 79d9c1435586d9b411b51a0ac395ea0c23dc3ddc && git merge --no-ff f972c24ced205938213adc96316ec3b08d055b0f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 79d9c1435586d9b411b51a0ac395ea0c23dc3ddc
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 79d9c1435586d9b411b51a0ac395ea0c23dc3ddc` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 维护者速读
修好主干变红：MySQL 上字段撤掉默认值后，不填该字段的写入不再被拒，改为存空值；三种数据库都在真实库上跑过。
原本"必填"的列不会被偷偷放宽：只有对象声明允许为空时，才连同放宽一起改，否则保持原样并在迁移计划里提示。
CI 全绿，223 行，非受管面，席位落地；合并后主干的 MySQL 实库测试会再验一遍。
要你做的：无。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT (L1) · repo:objectstack#1 · head `f972c24c` · 2026-11-23T02:32Z

- **Shape:** `Fixes #36596`; `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/schema-drift.ts`, `sql-driver-schema-sync.ts`, the #36245 test file (+4 NOT NULL cases, nothing removed or narrowed), one changeset. +215/−8. Tier S (`check-governed-merges`: 0 of 4 paths governed); no L2 face.
- **Premise corrected and measured** by the card thread on live MySQL 8.0.46: the column was nullable; MySQL 8's `DROP DEFAULT` leaves no default at all, so a strict-mode insert omitting it fails with ER 1364 where PG and SQLite store NULL. #36564's live evidence was MariaDB 10.11, which is why it passed there.
- **Read:** MySQL `drop_column_default` on a nullable column (`columnInfo().nullable`, read at apply time) is now `SET DEFAULT NULL`; NOT NULL keeps `DROP DEFAULT`. The differ no longer proposes a lone drop on a NOT NULL column: it pairs with the relax at `needs_confirm` when the declaration doesn't hold the column NOT NULL (publish/install apply the pair only for declared `storage.notNull: false`, via `isDeclaredRelaxPair`), else it is `destructive` and left alone with a message. The §3 pair case asserts, per cell, that the unset insert stores NULL after both ops are applied, so apply order and the stale `ci` read are covered on live MySQL.
- **Gates:** 57 checks on `f972c24c`: 39 success · 18 skipped · 0 failed; `landing-k` K = 7 < 15. Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL) is still path-filtered off PR runs; the thread ran the CI step's exact command in-container (MySQL 8.0.46, PG 16): the file 51/51 on all three cells; the full suite 7007 pass, 1 fail (the #11565 InnoDB page-limit case, which fails identically on main against that local server and is green in CI's image). Before the fix, the two §2 MySQL cases fail with ER 1364 on main `79d9c143`; the four ablations all go red.
- **Noted, not folded:** the CI path filter that keeps live cells off driver-sql PRs is a governed `ci.yml` edit and a CI-budget question; it goes to the maintainer as a separate card, not this PR. The cli.mdx publish paragraph and the MySQL MODIFY default on relax (pre-existing) are in the thread's report.
- **Landing:** ready + auto-merge now; main's push run is the live re-check.
